config.title: transform-origin

intro.title: transform-origin
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple interactive demo that rotates a square element to see how the point of rotation changes. You will learn the core concept of transform-origin, which controls the fixed point (like the center, corner, or edge) around which CSS transforms like rotation or scaling occur. The main technology involved is CSS, using the transform-origin property along with transform: rotate. By adjusting the transform-origin values, you'll visually explore how changing the origin point affects the element's movement, making your animations and transformations more precise and dynamic.
intro.usecase: The transform-origin property is essential for creating polished interactive UI elements in real-world applications. Developers use it to control rotation and scaling pivot points in dashboard widgets, such as rotating gauge needles around their base or expanding panels from specific corners. In modern interfaces, transform-origin enables realistic card flips in e-commerce product galleries, where cards rotate around their edges, and precise menu animations where dropdowns expand from their trigger points. This property is also crucial for creating loading spinners that rotate around their center and modal windows that scale up from their middle rather than awkwardly from a corner.

objectives: Apply the transform-origin property to modify the pivot point of CSS transformations
Configure different transform-origin values (keywords, percentages, length units) for precise control
Manipulate element rotation and scaling by adjusting the transform-origin point
Construct interactive examples that demonstrate how transform-origin affects transformation behavior
Integrate transform-origin with other CSS properties to create coordinated visual effects
Implement responsive transform-origin adjustments that adapt to different screen sizes
Control transformation origins for multiple elements within a single animation sequence

steps.title: Create a container element for the demonstration
steps.instruction: Create a div element with the class name 'transform-container' that will serve as the container for our transform-origin demonstration.
steps.hint: In CSS, you can create a class selector by starting with a dot (.) followed by the class name, then curly braces for the styles.
steps.expectedOutcome: A CSS class named 'transform-container' is created with an empty style block ready for properties.
successCriteria: The CSS file contains a class selector '.transform-container' with an opening and closing curly brace.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've created a class selector starting with a dot, followed by 'transform-container', and curly braces.
steps.feedbackWrong: create a CSS class named 'transform-container' using the correct selector syntax.

steps.title: Add a child element inside the container
steps.instruction: Inside the .transform-container class, add a child element with the class name 'transform-target' that will be the element we transform.
steps.hint: You can add a child element by creating a new CSS rule that targets .transform-target and placing it after the .transform-container rule.
steps.expectedOutcome: The CSS will have a .transform-target rule that can be styled separately from the container.
successCriteria: A CSS rule for .transform-target exists in the stylesheet.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've created a CSS rule with the exact class name 'transform-target'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The child element wasn't added correctly. Create a CSS rule for .transform-target to represent the element we'll transform.

steps.title: Style the container with basic dimensions and positioning
steps.instruction: Add width, height, and positioning styles to the .transform-container class to create a visible area for the demonstration.
steps.hint: Set width and height to fixed values (e.g., 300px and 200px) and use margin to center the container on the page.
steps.expectedOutcome: The container will have defined dimensions and be positioned visibly on the page.
successCriteria: The .transform-container rule includes width, height, and margin properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added some styles, but make sure to include width, height, and margin for full positioning.
steps.feedbackWrong: The container still lacks the necessary dimension and positioning styles. Try adding width, height, and margin properties.

steps.title: Style the transform element with initial appearance
steps.instruction: Add a CSS rule for the child element inside the container. Give it a width of 100px, height of 100px, a background color of #3498db, and a 2px solid black border.
steps.hint: Target the child element using the selector you created earlier, then add the width, height, background-color, and border properties.
steps.expectedOutcome: The child element will be visible as a blue square with a black border, ready for transformation.
successCriteria: The child element has width: 100px, height: 100px, background-color: #3498db, and border: 2px solid black.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've included all the required properties: width, height, background-color, and border.
steps.feedbackWrong: The styling isn't quite right. Check that you're targeting the child element and applying all the specified properties with the correct values.

steps.title: Apply a rotation transform to the element
steps.instruction: Add a CSS rule to rotate the child element by 45 degrees using the transform property.
steps.hint: Use the transform property with the rotate() function. The value should be 'rotate(45deg)'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The blue square element will be visibly rotated by 45 degrees, making the transform-origin effect more apparent in later steps.
successCriteria: The transform-element rule includes a transform property with rotate(45deg).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using the correct syntax: transform: rotate(45deg);
steps.feedbackWrong: The rotation transform wasn't applied correctly. Check that you've added 'transform: rotate(45deg);' to the .transform-element rule.

steps.title: Set the initial transform-origin to center
steps.instruction: Add the transform-origin property with value 'center' to the .transform-element rule to make it rotate around its center point.
steps.hint: The transform-origin property defines the point around which transformations like rotation occur. Use 'center' to set it to the middle of the element.
steps.expectedOutcome: The blue square will rotate around its center point when the rotation transform is applied in the next step.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've added transform-origin: center; to the .transform-element rule.
steps.feedbackWrong: The transform-origin property wasn't properly added. Check that you've written transform-origin: center; in the correct CSS rule.

steps.title: Change transform-origin to top-left corner
steps.instruction: In the .transform-element selector, change the transform-origin value from 'center' to 'top left'.
steps.hint: Replace 'center' with 'top left' in the transform-origin property.
steps.expectedOutcome: The element will rotate around its top-left corner instead of its center.
successCriteria: The .transform-element selector has transform-origin: top left;
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you changed 'center' to 'top left' in the transform-origin property.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check the transform-origin property in the .transform-element selector. It should be set to 'top left'.

steps.title: Use percentage values for transform-origin
steps.instruction: In the .transform-element rule, change the transform-origin value from 'center' to '25% 75%' to position the rotation point using percentages.
steps.hint: Replace 'center' with the percentage values '25% 75%' in the transform-origin property.
steps.expectedOutcome: The blue square will rotate around a point positioned at 25% from the left and 75% from the top of its own dimensions.
successCriteria: The .transform-element rule has transform-origin set to '25% 75%'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've changed the transform-origin value to exactly '25% 75%' (with a space between the values).
steps.feedbackWrong: The transform-origin value should be '25% 75%'. Check that you've replaced 'center' with these percentage values in the .transform-element rule.

steps.title: Add visual markers to show transform-origin position
steps.instruction: Add a pseudo-element to the .transform-element that visually marks the current transform-origin position with a small circle.
steps.hint: Use the ::before pseudo-element to create a small circle positioned at the transform-origin point. You can use absolute positioning and transform to center it.
steps.expectedOutcome: The transform element will have a small red circle at its center (the current transform-origin) to help visualize the rotation point.
successCriteria: The .transform-element selector includes a ::before pseudo-element that creates a small circular marker positioned at the transform-origin.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the pseudo-element is properly positioned at the transform-origin point.
steps.feedbackWrong: The visual marker isn't showing up correctly. Check that you've added the ::before pseudo-element with the correct properties.
